ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a uniform electric field with an electric field strength E of $1\times10^{2}\mathrm{V/m}$, a positive point charge with a charge of $2\times10^{-2}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B. It is known that the distance between points A and B is $L=2\mathrm{m}$, and the line connecting the two points makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the direction of the electric field.

1. Determine the potential difference ${U_{AB}}$ between points A and B.
2. Calculate the work done by the electric field force, $\mathrm{W_{AB}}$, during the movement of the charge from A to B.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In a uniform electric field with an electric field strength E of $1\times10^{2}\mathrm{V/m}$, a positive point charge with a charge of $2\times10^{-2}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B. It is known that the distance between points A and B is $L=2\mathrm{m}$, and the line connecting the two points makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the direction of the electric field. 1. Determine the potential difference ${U_{AB}}$ between points A and B. 2. Calculate the work done by the electric field force, $\mathrm{W_{AB}}$, during the movement of the charge from A to B.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The attached figure shows a set of parallel horizontal electric field lines, with all arrows pointing to the right, and labeled E; point A is at the lower left, point B is at the upper right, the dashed line AB points from A to B, and the angle between AB and the direction of the electric field is marked as 60° in the figure. Then reason: From A to B, the displacement projection along the direction of the electric field is L cos60°. Take E=1×10^2 V/m, L=2 m, therefore U_AB=E L cos60°=100×2×0.5=100 V. The charge q=2×10^-2 C, and the work done by the electric field force is W_AB=qU_AB=(2×10^-2)×100=2 J.
